The real measure of readiness is whether AI can participate in the design process without lowering quality, with human judgment remaining essential wherever tacit knowledge and context cannot be fully encoded.

articles.headline: Prioritize What Attackers Will Exploit: 4 Elements of Strong Exposure Prioritization
articles.blurb: Fewer than 10% of vulnerabilities are exploited, but remediation programs often treat most findings as urgent. Rank exposures using active-exploitation intelligence, asset criticality, EPSS-style exploitability modeling, and control validation. A vulnerability on an internet-facing system that handles regulated data, has known exploitation, and lacks segmentation should outrank a high-CVSS finding on an isolated internal asset. The model measures success by fewer exploitable exposures and reduced remediation effort, rather than ticket volume.

articles.headline: The Quiet Phase: Why Active Directory Group Enumeration Deserves Your Attention
articles.blurb: Attackers map who sits in Domain Admins with SharpHound or PowerView long before they change any group membership, and an audit entry (SACL) on the group's member attribute turns those reads into Event 4662, or 4799 for built-in groups, on the domain controller that answered. On real privileged groups, the signal drowns in reads from directory sync, Exchange, and admin tooling, and SAMR-based tools like net group /domain bypass it entirely. Pair the audit with decoy groups that nothing legitimate ever reads, correlate a decoy read and a real admin-group read from the same logon session, and check coverage with its QuietPhase PowerShell script.

articles.headline: Jailbreaking my car's navigation system just so I can change the time
articles.blurb: A Renault Latitude's TomTom Carminat LIVE head unit hid its clock settings behind a legitimate navigation SD card. The card used CID-based DRM and signed files, so a blank card could not supply the missing menu definition. The author reverse-engineered the Linux 2.6.28 firmware, built a QEMU and CAN emulator, and found that master.script allowed a root path-traversal write through its LOG command and wrote |/bin/sh /media/sdcard/payload.sh into /proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern, then crashed /bin/dbus-monitor to trigger a coredump and execute the payload as root. The exploit enabled an eMMC backup and a timezone patch from UTC+3 to UTC+2.

It blocks calls to undeclared tools and calls that reach hosts nobody mentioned in the conversation, and it runs atif-scan detectors that catch reads of /proc/1/environ or curl --noproxy. Ambiguous calls can go to an optional judge model that sees only the user's prompt, the call, and the findings, never the agent's reasoning, and it works with any harness that accepts a custom base URL, including Claude Code, OpenCode, and Hermes.
